what: Forward propagation cost of all four engines on the workload the trainer actually runs: observable X_5, the production L=3 trained angles, delta=1e-6.
why: results/4x4/gpu_benchmark.json part A compares sorted-numpy against sorted-cupy. It never compares either against the string-dict engine that src/bppps/trainer.py imports, so it does not say what training would gain. This does.
caveat: Forward only. propagate_backward has no numba/sorted/cupy port at all, and the adjoint is the larger half: at L=3 production angles a full gradient evaluation over 32 observables measured 40.1 s forward against 84.1 s backward. Wiring the trainer to a faster engine therefore requires writing the adjoint for it; the forward speedup alone caps out at about 1.5x on the whole step.

term_count_is_angle_sensitive.note: The evolved SPO size depends steeply on angle magnitude, so any cost estimate taken at warm-start angles is meaningless.
